newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Monetary committee urges Italian pension reform.
newsitem.headline: Monetary committee urges Italian pension reform.

text.p: The European Union's monetary committee on Wednesday urged Italy to engage in additional reforms to its pensions systems, EU sources said.
Meeting to review Italy's efforts to consolidate its public finances ahead of economic and monetary union, the group was generally encouraged by Rome's efforts.
"It was well received," an EU official told Reuters.
The official added that the committee, made up of national treasury and central bank official, recommended "structural reforms in the pension area."

Italy's hopes of joining the first wave of countries inside monetary union in 1999 have been bolstered by expectations that the Maastricht Treaty's criteria for deficits and debt will be applied more flexibly.
On Tuesday the Italian Senate -- the upper house of parliament -- approved the centre-left government's three-year programme of key economic targets.
The financial plan sets out strict targets for 1998-2000 to keep Italy on course to join Europe's planned single currency.
EU monetary affairs commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy on Wednesday said the Italian economy was moving in the right direction ahead of the single currency's planned start.
But he added that Italy's 1998 budget would be a key element in determining whether the country qualified for EMU on schedule.
EU finance ministers will meet on July 7 to consider Italy's economic convergence programme.
